title: SSH private keys
whyItMatters: Private keys in this folder grant access to servers and Git hosts without a password. They must be rotated if the machine changes hands.
source: OpenSSH ssh(1) manual, FILES: ~/.ssh holds per-user keys and configuration; macforensics.app cheat sheet (SSH)
notes: macOS uses the same ~/.ssh layout as Linux. Key material is never opened; known_hosts and config are included in the count only.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy any key you still rely on to encrypted storage off this Mac, then plan replacements.
cleanup.signOut: Remove this Mac's public key from every server's authorized keys file and from each Git host account.
steps: List the public keys in the folder named in the plan and where each is installed.
Remove those public keys from servers, cloud consoles and Git hosts.
Delete the folder named in the plan, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Servers that accepted only these keys deny access until new keys are added; unremoved keys still work.
cleanup.source: OpenSSH manual, ssh(1), FILES section: https://man.openbsd.org/ssh
